summary: Three static reply-thread placement options for NoteDetailView, spread along a deliberate disclosure-distance axis with each entry affordance in a different screen region: (A) inline continuation -- a second gold hairline plus 'REPLIES' label and stacked cards in the empty ground below the note body, no new chrome; (B) docked bottom drawer -- a persistent gradientPill count bar above the safe area raising a radiusXXL 36 medium-detent sheet over the dimmed body; (C) pushed thread screen -- a ghostPill count chip with monogram cluster in the toolbar opening a full NavigationStack destination with a pinned composer. All three share one locked palette drawn entirely from existing Theme tokens (bgPage #1E1812, cardBg #221508 @0.90, borderGoldDim, topEdgeHighlight elevation, goldGradient, textGold #D4922A) and one governing idea -- authorship contrast: the note stays un-carded, full-bleed and serif per the existing Direction B decision, while replies arrive as .widgetCard-contained, Inter sans-serif objects with gold-gradient monogram avatars. Empty state is identical to today's screen in all three. Rendered as six real SwiftUI simulator captures at 1260x2736 (populated + second state per option) plus one composition sheet on a #151009 ground -- not OpenArt, matching the -continue-button-circle-icon-options precedent. Verified contrast forbids textGoldMuted (2.94:1) and textMuted (2.30:1) for reply text on cardBg. Two risks surfaced on the sheet itself: personal notes have no wired GET-replies endpoint (only group notes do), and Option B collides with the documented sheet-on-a-sheet compact-adaptation regression at NotesListView.swift:851-871, whose existing .fullScreenCover escape hatch is incompatible with a partial detent.
